criteria.quote: "Beedrill has three stingers, but one is worst."
criteria.revision: Change the opening narration to: "Beedrill has three poison barbs—but only its tail barb secretes the most powerful poison." This states the evidence-backed anomaly immediately and avoids the vague word "worst."

criteria.quote: "Two poisonous stingers sit on Beedrill's forelegs, part of three."
criteria.revision: Make the anatomy contrast more direct: "Two poison barbs are on its forelegs. The third is on its tail." This better sets up the specific tail-versus-foreleg reveal.

criteria.quote: "If all three stingers are poisonous, why is the tail barb worse?"
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported implied explanation question with an evidence-grounded comparison question: "All three are poisonous—so which barb carries Beedrill's most powerful poison?" The answer is explicitly supported by the Silver entry.

criteria.quote: "Those three poisonous stingers can jab an enemy repeatedly." / "Then Beedrill flies at high speed, striking with its stingers."
criteria.revision: Reorder and tighten the middle so it builds toward the reveal: first establish the three-barb layout, then say "It can jab an enemy repeatedly," then "It can strike with poison needles at high speed before flying off," and reserve the tail's stronger poison as the final factual reveal. Remove repeated generic references to "stingers" where possible.

criteria.quote: "But its tail barb secretes the most powerful poison."
criteria.revision: Delay the exact location until the reveal and sharpen the contrast: "The foreleg barbs are poisonous too. But Beedrill's most powerful poison comes from the barb on its tail."

criteria.quote: Two poisonous stingers sit on Beedrill's forelegs, part of three.
criteria.revision: Scene "foreleg-pair" repeats scene "three-stingers". Replace it with a new step in the story.

criteria.quote: "Beedrill can jab repeatedly with all three stingers, but its tail barb carries the most powerful poison."
criteria.revision: Make the payoff answer the opening comparison cleanly: "All three poison barbs can jab repeatedly. But the tail barb is the outlier: it secretes Beedrill's most powerful poison."

criteria.quote: "Foreleg stingers or tail barb: which threat scares you most?"
criteria.revision: Use a more evidence-tied split: "Would you fear the two foreleg barbs that can jab repeatedly—or the tail barb with Beedrill's most powerful poison?"
